references.text: Nicodemus is mentioned again here as the one who previously came to Jesus at night ([ref:Joh 7:50-52|John 7:50-52]), and defended him before the Pharisees.
Nicodemus is identified again as the one who first came to Jesus at night ([ref:Joh 19:39|John 19:39]), when he brought spices for Jesus' burial.
The Pharisees discuss whether Jesus is from God, referring to the signs he performs – the same reasoning Nicodemus uses ([ref:Joh 9:16|John 9:16]).
The man born blind argues in a similar way as Nicodemus: If this man were not from God, he could do nothing ([ref:Joh 9:33|John 9:33]).

Many believed in Jesus' name when they saw the signs he performed – this forms the background for Nicodemus' statement that no one can perform such signs unless God is with him ([ref:Joh 2:23|John 2:23]).
Jesus' first sign at Cana revealed his glory. Nicodemus acknowledges that Jesus' signs testify to his divine origin ([ref:Joh 2:11|John 2:11]).

Peter testifies that Jesus of Nazareth was a man appointed by God, confirmed through mighty works, wonders and signs which God did through him – the same line of thought Nicodemus expresses ([ref:Apg 2:22|Acts 2:22]).
Peter proclaims that God was with Jesus – a parallel to Nicodemus' recognition that God must be with the one who performs such signs ([ref:Apg 10:38|Acts 10:38]).
The title "Rabbi" is also used by the disciples when they first meet Jesus ([ref:Joh 1:38|John 1:38]), showing that Nicodemus recognizes Jesus as a teacher.
The motif of night: Judas went out, "and it was night" ([ref:Joh 13:30|John 13:30]). John uses night and darkness symbolically, and Nicodemus comes to Jesus precisely at night.

The light and darkness motif is further developed later in the conversation: people loved darkness more than light. Nicodemus' nighttime visit can be seen in light of this ([ref:Joh 3:19-21|John 3:19-21]).
God promises Moses: "I will be with you" ([ref:2 Mos 3:12|Exodus 3:12]). Nicodemus uses the same idea – God is with the one he sends – to explain Jesus' signs.

After the feeding miracle, the people say that Jesus is the prophet who was to come into the world, based on the sign they had seen ([ref:Joh 6:14|John 6:14]) – a sign as proof of divine sending, just as Nicodemus reasons.
